headline: Solid quarter as guidance holds, data-center pipeline grows
summary_short: PPL's second-quarter 2026 GAAP earnings rose 26% y/y to $230M ($0.30/share diluted), with ongoing (non-GAAP) EPS up 3% to $0.33; the company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 ongoing EPS forecast of $1.90-$1.98 (midpoint $1.94).
summary_long: Operating revenue rose 4.2% y/y to $2,111M and operating income rose 17.0% to $475M, as higher Kentucky retail rates and higher Pennsylvania transmission revenue offset a 1.6% decline in electricity sales volumes. Higher depreciation and interest expense (long-term debt $19.8B vs $18.0B at year-end) partly offset the gains. PPL reaffirmed its FY2026 ongoing EPS range of $1.90-$1.98 (midpoint $1.94) and its 6%-8% long-term EPS growth target through 2029, citing improving second-half rate recovery. Cash fell to $332M from $1,071M as YTD capex of $2,339M outspent $1,140M of operating cash flow, funded partly by $2,046M of new debt issuance. Management flagged $10-12B of potential Pennsylvania/Kentucky data-center generation-investment upside through 2032, separate from guidance.

drivers.explanation: Segment mix: Kentucky +$0.01 (higher retail rates, offset by opex/depreciation/interest); Pennsylvania -$0.02 (higher depreciation/interest, partly offset by transmission revenue); Rhode Island +$0.03 (lower opex, higher rider revenue); Corporate +$0.03 (lower net special-item charges).
Tracks the diluted EPS move; basic shares (752.4M) rose less than the dilutive share count, leaving basic growth (24%) modestly ahead of diluted growth (20%).
Segment ongoing mix: Kentucky flat; Pennsylvania -$0.01 (higher depreciation/interest); Rhode Island +$0.02 (lower opex, higher rider revenue); Corporate flat.
Reflects the same segment-level drivers as diluted EPS, applied to a weighted-average diluted share count of 757.2M versus 742.5M a year ago.
Grew in line with ongoing EPS growth; net special-item charges of $17M this quarter were smaller than $57M a year ago, mostly IT-transformation and integration costs.

Higher Kentucky retail rates effective Jan 1, 2026 and higher Pennsylvania transmission revenue from added capital investment drove revenue up despite a 1.6% y/y decline in total electricity sales volumes.
Revenue growth of 4.2% outpaced total operating expense growth of 1.0%, lifting operating income 17.0%.
Segment YTD moves: Kentucky +$0.06, Pennsylvania -$0.02, Rhode Island -$0.01, Corporate +$0.07, the last driven mainly by lower net special-item charges ($43M YTD 2026 vs $87M YTD 2025).

Segment YTD ongoing moves: Kentucky +$0.03 (higher retail rates and capital returns, partly offset by lower sales volumes and higher costs), Pennsylvania -$0.01, Rhode Island +$0.01, Corporate +$0.01.
Reaffirmed unchanged based on year-to-date performance; company expects stronger second-half 2026 growth from improved rate recovery and capital tracking mechanisms.

CEO Vincent Sorgi cited disciplined cost management, timely recovery of investments, and constructive regulatory frameworks; management also highlighted a growing Pennsylvania/Kentucky data-center pipeline as a long-term (not current-quarter) growth driver, estimating $10-12B of incremental investment upside through 2032.
